title: Generation of Functional Mouse Hippocampal Neurons
author: Francesco Tomassoni-Ardori

steps.title: Coat dishes with poly‑D‑lysine
steps.instruction: Reconstitute poly‑D‑lysine (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # P6407) by adding 50 ml sterile tissue‑culture‑grade water to a 5 mg γ‑irradiated bottle to obtain a 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ working solution; evenly cover each culture surface (e.g., 12 mm round coverslips, Corning, cat # 354087, or 24‑well plate wells) with the solution and incubate at room temperature for 20 min in a laminar flow hood; aspirate the solution and rinse twice with sterile water; allow the surface to dry completely uncovered for ~1 h before use.

steps.title: Prepare poly‑D‑lysine/laminin coverslips
steps.instruction: If using pre‑coated poly‑D‑lysine/laminin 12 mm coverslips (Corning, cat # 354087) transfer them directly into wells of a 24‑well plate with sterile forceps; alternatively, coat regular 12 mm coverslips with 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ poly‑D‑lysine for 20 min, wash twice with PBS, then cover with 10 µg ml⁻¹ laminin (Thermo Fisher, cat # 23017‑015) for ≥4 h at 37 °C in an incubator; rinse twice with PBS immediately before plating cells. The laminin stock (1 mg ml⁻¹) is made by adding 1 ml PBS to 1 mg laminin powder and diluting to 10 µg ml⁻¹ with PBS.

steps.title: Sacrifice pregnant mouse and collect embryos
steps.instruction: Euthanize the pregnant mouse according to ACUC‑approved protocol (CO₂ or isoflurane followed by decapitation or cervical dislocation); pin the animal, clean abdomen with 70 % ethanol, make a mid‑abdominal incision with surgical scissors, and expose the uterine horns. Transfer the uterus to a 100 mm dish containing ice‑cold PBS.

steps.title: Isolate embryo heads in cold DMEM
steps.instruction: Using forceps, pull the uterus out while cutting connective tissue and cervix; free individual embryos, remove placenta and yolk sac, and place embryos in a new 100 mm dish with ice‑cold DMEM (Thermo Fisher, cat # 11965‑092) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS, non‑heat‑inactivated, Omega Scientific, cat # FB‑01) and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (P/S, 10 000 U ml⁻¹, Thermo Fisher, cat # 15140‑122). Using forceps, hold each embryo head and cut off the head with surgical scissors; transfer heads to a fresh dish containing the same complete DMEM.

steps.title: Dissect brains and isolate hippocampi
steps.instruction: In a sterile laminar flow cabinet, prepare a 100 mm dish with ice‑cold complete DMEM. Transfer one embryo head at a time, pinch the mouth/nose area with forceps, and insert fine scissors (Figure 1C) from the back of the skull to make a transverse cut at the mouth/nose level, freeing the basal brain region. Invert the head, pull apart the skull with two forceps, and remove the whole brain. Transfer brains to a new 100 mm dish with fresh ice‑cold complete DMEM, changing the medium after each brain.

steps.title: Remove meninges from brain hemispheres
steps.instruction: Place a brain in a 35 mm dish lid filled with ice‑cold complete DMEM under a stereoscope; using two Dumont forceps (Figure 1E), hold the brain with one forceps and gently peel off the meninges with the other, starting at the olfactory bulb and moving posteriorly until meninges are fully removed.

steps.title: Transfer hippocampi to serum‑free DMEM
steps.instruction: Using curved forceps (Figure 1D), separate the two hemispheres, flip them to expose the hippocampal region, and finely cut along the hippocampal edges with Dumont forceps. Pick each C‑shaped hippocampus with curved forceps and transfer it to a 35 mm tissue‑culture dish containing 2 ml ice‑cold serum‑free DMEM (DMEM without FBS, supplemented with 1 % P/S).

steps.title: Mince hippocampal tissue
steps.instruction: In the same 35 mm dish, mince each hippocampus into 5–6 pieces of ~2–3 mm³ using two Dumont forceps (Figure 6C). Keep the minced tissue in the serum‑free DMEM to avoid inhibition of subsequent trypsin activity.

steps.title: Trypsin digestion of hippocampal pieces
steps.instruction: Transfer the medium with minced hippocampi to a 50 ml sterile conical tube; add 2 ml of 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA (Thermo Fisher, cat # 25200‑056) to achieve a final trypsin concentration of 0.125 %; place the tube in a 37 °C water bath for 25 min. During digestion, tissue will settle by gravity.

steps.title: Neutralize trypsin with serum medium
steps.instruction: Prepare a 15 ml sterile conical tube containing 2 ml warm (37 °C) DMEM complete with 10 % FBS and 1 % P/S. After digestion, return the 50 ml tube to the hood, avoid disturbing the sediment, and using a 1 ml pipette tip, gently aspirate only the hippocampal pellet and transfer it to the 15 ml tube. The serum in the 2 ml medium inactivates the trypsin.

steps.title: Fire‑polish Pasteur pipettes for trituration
steps.instruction: Using a Bunsen burner, fire‑polish a sterile glass Pasteur pipette to create a smaller, smooth tip (Figure 7B) for the first trituration; prepare a second fire‑polished pipette with a longer tapered tip (Figure 7C) for the second trituration.

steps.title: First trituration (6‑8 passes)
steps.instruction: With the first fire‑polished pipette, gently pipet the hippocampal suspension up and down 6–8 times until tissue chunks are completely broken up. Allow the pipette to cool before use.

steps.title: Second trituration to single cells
steps.instruction: Using the second tapered fire‑polished pipette, perform a single gentle up‑and‑down motion to obtain a single‑cell suspension. Proceed immediately to cell counting; avoid excessive pipetting to preserve viability.

steps.title: Assess viability with Trypan blue
steps.instruction: Mix 50 µl of the cell suspension with 5 µl of Trypan blue (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # 93595) and count live versus dead cells using a Cellometer disposable counting slide (Nexcelom, cat # CHT4‑SD100‑002). Expected viability is 70–90 % (e.g., 4 × 10⁶ live cells from 5 × 10⁶ total for 8 embryos).

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend cells in Neurobasal
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the remaining cell suspension at 350 × g for 5 min; discard supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in warm Neurobasal medium (Thermo Fisher, cat # 21103‑049) containing B27 supplement (Thermo Fisher, cat # 17504‑044). Adjust the final volume to achieve a seeding density of ~260 000 cells cm⁻² for the chosen culture vessel.

steps.title: Prepare complete Neurobasal medium
steps.instruction: For 500 ml Neurobasal, add 10 ml B27 supplement and 5 ml P/S (100× concentrate, Thermo Fisher, cat # 15140‑122) to obtain 2 % B27 and 1 % antibiotics. This medium will be used for plating and subsequent culture.

steps.title: Seed neurons at defined density
steps.instruction: Plate the cell suspension onto the poly‑D‑lysine‑coated dishes or poly‑D‑lysine/laminin‑coated 12 mm coverslips placed in a 24‑well plate, using the calculated volume to reach ~260 000 cells cm⁻². Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Add Ara‑C to suppress proliferation
steps.instruction: 18–24 h after plating, remove half of the culture medium and replace it with fresh Neurobasal + B27 containing 2 µM cytosine arabinoside (Ara‑C; stock 50 mg ml⁻¹ in water, stored at –20 °C, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # C6645) to achieve a final concentration of 1 µM. This step reduces non‑neuronal cell proliferation.

steps.title: Half‑medium changes every 48‑72 h
steps.instruction: Replace only 50 % of the culture medium with fresh Neurobasal + B27 every 48–72 h. Do not add additional Ara‑C after the initial treatment.

steps.title: Harvest neurons for western blot
steps.instruction: At day 6 in vitro, aspirate medium from one well of a 24‑well plate, rinse cells once with DPBS (Thermo Fisher, cat # 14190‑144), and add 150 µl 2× Laemmli sample buffer (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # S3401) directly to the well. Transfer lysate to a 1.5 ml tube, sonicate for 10 min, heat at 95 °C for 5 min, load 10 µl per lane on a 4–12 % NuPAGE Bis‑Tris gel (Thermo Fisher, cat # NP0321PK2), run at 120 V, transfer to a PVDF membrane, block with 5 % non‑fat milk in TBS‑Tween 0.1 % for 1 h at RT, incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies (e.g., anti‑TrkB, anti‑Rbfox1, anti‑β‑III‑tubulin, anti‑NeuN; all Millipore, cat # 07‑225, MABE985, MAB377 respectively) diluted 1:1 000 in 5 % milk/TBS‑Tween, wash 3 × 5 min, incubate 1 h at RT with HRP‑conjugated secondary antibodies (anti‑mouse HRP, cat # AP192P; anti‑rabbit HRP, cat # AP182P) diluted 1:5 000, wash 3 × 5 min, develop with SuperSignal West Dura substrate (Thermo Fisher, cat # 34076) and image.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining of neurons
steps.instruction: After 6 days, remove medium from coverslip‑containing wells, rinse with PBS, and fix with 4 % paraformaldehyde (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # P6148) in PBS for 30 min at 4 °C. Rinse with calcium/magnesium‑free PBS (PBS‑/‑) 3 × 5 min. Block for 1 h at RT in blocking solution containing 10 % normal donkey serum (v/v), 0.1 % Triton X‑100 (v/v, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # T8532), and 0.1 % BSA (w/v, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat # A9647) in PBS‑/‑. Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies diluted in 1 % donkey serum, 0.1 % Triton X‑100, 0.1 % BSA in PBS‑/‑: anti‑GFAP (Agilent/Dako, cat # Z0334) 1:1 000 and anti‑β‑III‑tubulin (Covance, cat # MMS‑435P) 1:200. Rinse 3 × 5 min with PBS‑/‑, then incubate 2 h at RT with secondary antibodies and DAPI (Invitrogen, cat # D1306) 0.5 µg ml⁻¹: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti‑rabbit IgG (Thermo Fisher, cat # A‑21206) for GFAP and Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti‑mouse IgG (Thermo Fisher, cat # A‑31571) for β‑III‑tubulin, both diluted 1:250 in the same blocking solution. Rinse 3 × 5 min, invert coverslips onto glass slides, mount with Dako fluorescence mounting medium (cat # S3023), let dry, and image by confocal microscopy.

steps.title: Calcium imaging with Fluo‑4
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 ml Fluo‑4 loading buffer: 1 µl 1 mM Fluo‑4 (Thermo Fisher, cat # F14217) + 10 µl PowerLoad (100×, Thermo Fisher, cat # P10020) + 10 µl Probenecid (stock 250 mM, Thermo Fisher, cat # P36400) + 979 µl ECS buffer (140 mM NaCl, 4.7 mM KCl, 2 mM NaHCO₃, 1 mM NaH₂PO₄, 1.2 mM MgCl₂, 1.5 mM CaCl₂, 3 mM glucose, 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4). After day 6, remove medium from each coverslip, add 250 µl loading buffer, incubate at 37 °C for 30 min, then wash with 250 µl ECS buffer at 37 °C for 30 min to allow de‑esterification. Place coverslip in a recording chamber with flow 0.5 ml min⁻¹, temperature 37 °C. Acquire confocal images at 2 frames s⁻¹ (pixel dwell time set so acquisition <500 ms) using 480 nm laser at minimal intensity. After baseline recording, apply 1 mM glutamate for 10 s to depolarize cells. Analyze data in ImageJ/Fiji: set LUT to Rainbow RGB, adjust brightness/contrast, open ROI manager, draw ROIs around individual neurons, use "Plot Z‑axis Profile" to obtain fluorescence over time, export plots for quantification.
